text:
jess: FYI opened a docs PR to add a small 'Sample Prompt Set' + embed usage note to the Nebula3b model card — https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321. Need quick eyes on embed limits, SDK snippet, and a short SLA blurb. @omar @kai @maya

omar: on it. quick q — current limits table in the card lists 'embedding max_len: 2048' but our bench data for shard/embedding suggests 1024. which should we show?

jess: bench numbers I used are from last week's run on dedicated pools (results attached to the PR). I'm pretty sure 1024 is the safe published value, we can add a note about sharded embeddings for >1024.

kai: agree 1024 is safer. also the python SDK snippet in the model card still uses `max_len` param — SDK v3 renamed that to `max_tokens`. I'll push a small snippet patch unless you want to coordinate.

maya: one editorial note — we should avoid committing SLA-like language in model cards w/out product signoff. Keep a single-sentence 'expected latency range under dedicated capacity' and link to the SLA doc instead of hard guarantees.

jess: good call. I'll redact the stronger phrasing and replace with: "Expected p95 generation latency on Dedicated: ~120-180ms (depends on sequence length); see SLA for details." That should be safe.

omar: docsbot flagged a lint/link issue: anchor mismatch for the embedding section — PR links to `#embedding-shard` but the header is `Embedding Shard Usage` which would produce `#embedding_shard`.

docsbot: lint error: MD013/trailing spaces in model_card.md: lines 78-80. Also suggested anchor fix: replace `#embedding-shard` with `#embedding_shard` or add an explicit anchor.

kai: I'll update the snippet to use the new param and add a short comment about sharding. Proposed Python snippet (will push to branch):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
# embedding example — shard if >1024 tokens
resp = client.embeddings.create(model='nebula3b', input=text, max_tokens=1024)
```

jess: nice and concise. Could we include a tiny JS example too? Some customers only scan JS snippets.

kai: sure — will add JS similarly: `client.embeddings.create({ model: 'nebula3b', input, max_tokens: 1024 })`

maya: editorial nit — for accessibility, call out the link to the benchmark CSV and add a 1-line summary under 'Benchmarks' (e.g., median throughput and p95 latency at 512 tokens). Keeps the card readable for non-technical reviewers.

omar: adding bench link is good. I can also add a short compatibility note: 'quantized variants are supported on Dedicated and Private; CPU fallback via edge-quant is experimental and may present higher latency'. This helps set expectations.

jess: perfect. Once kai's snippet + my SLA sentence + omar's compatibility line & the anchor fix are in, can someone run the doc linter and then we can merge?

ci-bot: build/docs-lint — started for PR #4321. ETA ~2m.

docsbot: pre-merge checklist: 1) anchor/link fixes ✅ 2) snippet param updated ✅ 3) bench link added ✅ 4) SLA sentence reviewed by product — pending (tag product@pm)

maya: I can ping product in the thread after CI passes. product review should be quick for a 1-line change.

jess: cool — I'll hold the PR open until product confirms. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround — this was mainly proofreading + tiny SDK change vs large content edits, so should be fast.

omar: quick follow-up: do we want to add a short migration note in the SDK snippets section: 'if you previously used `max_len`, change to `max_tokens` — values are identical' ? saves confusion.

kai: yes adding that now. I'll push one more commit to the PR with both Python/JS examples and the migration note.

jess: sweet. tagging this thread as 'ready-for-prod-review' once product signs off. :thumbsup:
